_doc: Round 9 cello per-note table (size 2.1): gain_db = dB on each partial's output gain, dark_db = dB added to its onset darkening, loss_add = 1/s added to its released loss, drop_db = its own drop at the let-go (over rdk_s); the scalars replace the value at the cello's size (before its size powers). Read at note-on by the nearest MIDI note; held at first below, faded out over fade_above semitones above last. Round 10: gain_db refitted (one damped step on partial levels, seeds 1-2); hf_add = dB on the string's top (hf_db, -100: off); cflr_add = dB on the low floor (cflr_db). Round 11: kn_on [8 octave columns, centres 110 Hz to 14 kHz][6 knots at 0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.35, 0.6 s from the note-on; 0 at 0.9 s and after] and kn_rl [8][5 knots at 0.05, 0.15, 0.3, 0.45, 0.6 s after the let-go; 0 at the let-go, held after the last] = dB on each partial's gain, interpolated over the partials in log frequency (fitted with the bow frozen on seeds 1-2). Round 12: kn_on/kn_rl refitted (a second frozen-bow pass, increments added, with the layers in place); rs0_db, rs1_db, rs2_db = the residual layers' band energies (dB, look.py's 45 bands as the score's STFT reads them, at an envelope of 1; -200: none): sustain, onset, release, as the violin's, played by w t and replacing the low floor, the string's top and the release floor; rs_env = this table's own layer envelope (rs0_rdb 20, rs0_att 0.4, the rest the violin's); sn_db = the sine wander's depth (dB, replaces 3.7854), am_db = the level vibrato's depth (dB, replaces 1.8913).
